sources.entry: Bifrost - A tiny terminal emulator for serial port communication (macOS/Linux).

summary.one_liner: Bifrost is a tiny terminal emulator for talking to serial port devices, with binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: Bifrost opens a serial port and acts as a terminal emulator for serial communication. It takes a -port-path flag (default /dev/tty.usbserial) and a -baud flag (default 115200). The README says it supports USB type-C out of the box and is friendly to 2016+ MacBooks. Prebuilt binaries are distributed as zip files from the releases page. The README gives install steps for Linux (copy to /usr/bin), macOS (copy to /usr/local/bin), and Windows (add a PowerShell alias). It also says to run bifrost -help to confirm installation.
use_cases: Connect to a device over a USB serial adapter
Talk to embedded boards or microcontrollers from the terminal
Open a serial console on a MacBook
Set a custom serial port path and baud rate
Use a serial terminal on Linux or Windows
how_to_run: Download the latest zip for your platform from the releases page
Linux: unzip, then sudo cp bifrost /usr/bin/ and set owner root:root and mode 755
macOS: sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin, unzip, then sudo cp bifrost /usr/local/bin/
Windows: unzip to a folder and create a PowerShell alias pointing to bifrost.exe
Run bifrost -help to confirm the install
stack: Go (inferred from linux-amd64 and darwin-amd64 binary naming; not stated in README)
notable: Single small binary with no install dependencies stated
Designed for USB type-C and 2016+ MacBooks
Configurable port path and baud rate flags
caveats: The README does not state a license
Default port path /dev/tty.usbserial is macOS-style and must be changed on Linux
Windows setup requires manual PowerShell alias configuration
